refactor.title: One home for the slug-or-id lookup and the slug-on-update logic of groups and households
refactor.text:
RepositoryGroup (mealie/repos/repository_group.py) and RepositoryHousehold (mealie/repos/repository_household.py) each carry their own copy of the same two pieces of logic:
- get_by_slug_or_id: take a slug or an id (a UUID or its string form) and return the matching record;
- update: re-derive the slug from the name before saving.

Put each piece of logic in one place that both repositories use, so that a change to it is made once. This is a refactor: behavior must not change. Both repositories keep the same public methods with the same signatures and the same results, and every existing test still passes.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (the whole backend suite, about 9 minutes). For quicker loops while you work, tests/unit_tests/repository_tests and tests/integration_tests/admin_tests cover these repositories.

measured.chosenBy: a normalized-AST duplicate scan of mealie/ at the base commit; the largest pair of duplicated methods shared by two classes of one layer

fix.text:
Security report: two weaknesses in Mealie's external login providers.

1. OIDC trusts email addresses the identity provider has not verified. With OpenID Connect login on, OpenIDProvider.authenticate() matches and creates accounts by the email claim even when the claims say the address is unverified ("email_verified": false) or say nothing about it. Since an existing Mealie account is matched by its email, anyone who can register an unverified address at the identity provider can log into the Mealie account that uses that address.
   Expected: a new setting OIDC_REQUIRES_EMAIL_VERIFICATION (environment variable; default true). While it is true, authenticate() raises MissingClaimException unless the claims carry "email_verified" set to true, for new and existing accounts alike. Set to false, logins work as they do today.

2. LDAP:
   a. A login with an empty password succeeds against directories that treat a bind with a valid DN and an empty password as an anonymous bind, so anyone could log in as a known user. An empty password must be refused before any bind: the provider's get_user() returns None.
   b. The username goes into the LDAP search filter unescaped, so a username such as `a*)(uid=*` rewrites the filter (LDAP injection). The username must be escaped wherever it enters a filter (RFC 4515: `*` becomes `\2a`, and so on for `(`, `)`, `\` and NUL).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/core/security/providers/test_openid_provider.py tests/unit_tests/test_security.py`; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 9 minutes).

debug.text:
Bug report: models that declare their own auto_init exclusions lose primary-key protection.

Mealie's SQLAlchemy models are initialised through the @auto_init() decorator, which copies the incoming keyword data onto the row and skips the keys in its configuration's exclude set. By default that set is {"id"}, so an id in the incoming data never overwrites a primary key. Models with a model_config = ConfigDict(exclude={...}) of their own (foods, groups, households, shopping-list items, ...) are not protected: an id in the data passed to them, or to their nested one-to-many elements on update, is written onto the row.

Find the cause and fix it. Expected: a model's own exclude adds to the default exclusions instead of replacing them. The configuration auto_init resolves for a model class (_get_config(cls) in the decorator's module, an AutoInitConfig) has exclude equal to {"id"} together with the model's own entries ("id" once if the model lists it too); a class without a model_config, or whose model_config sets other keys only (such as get_attr), keeps exclude == {"id"}.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 9 minutes).

quick.text:
Bug: a food or unit whose description is NULL in the database breaks the API.

Foods and units created by older versions or by imports can have a NULL description column. Reading one fails: the IngredientFood and IngredientUnit schemas declare description as a string, so validating such a row raises a pydantic ValidationError.

Expected: IngredientFood.model_validate(row) and IngredientUnit.model_validate(row) accept a row whose description is None and give description == ""; a non-empty description is kept as it is.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 9 minutes).

feature.text:
Feature: OIDC login for native (mobile and desktop) clients.

Mealie's OIDC login works only in a browser: GET /api/auth/oauth redirects to the identity provider and GET /api/auth/oauth/callback finishes the login with the session cookie. Native apps have to log in through the system browser (passkey-only providers such as Pocket ID do not work in embedded WebViews), run their own PKCE authorization request, catch the authorization code at a redirect URI of their own, and then need Mealie to exchange that code. Add two public endpoints for that, available whenever OIDC is configured (no new setting):

- GET /api/auth/oauth/native/config returns what a client needs to build its authorization request: authorization_endpoint (from the provider's metadata), client_id and scope.
- POST /api/auth/oauth/native/token takes JSON {code, code_verifier, redirect_uri, nonce (optional)}, exchanges the code with the provider through the same registered authlib client the web flow uses (oauth.create_client("oidc"): fetch_access_token with the code, code_verifier and redirect_uri, then parse_id_token with the nonce), finds or creates the user from the claims the way the web callback does, and answers with a Mealie access token in the same shape as the other login responses.

Errors: while OIDC is not configured both endpoints answer 404 with detail "OIDC is not configured". A code the provider rejects (authlib raises OAuthError) is a 401. Anything else (an unreachable provider, an id_token that fails validation, whose joserfc errors are not OAuthError) is not turned into a 401: it stays a server error (500), as on the web callback.

Put the endpoints in the module of the web OIDC routes (GET /api/auth/oauth and /oauth/callback) and use that module's settings and oauth objects: tests replace them. Add the request and response schemas next to the other auth schemas, the matching TypeScript types to the frontend's API types, and a section on the native flow to the OIDC documentation page (the native client registers its redirect URI on the same OIDC client at the provider).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 9 minutes).

routes.text:
Feature: a connectivity test for a group's AI providers.

Group managers configure AI providers (base_url, api_key, model, ...) under /api/groups/ai-providers, but learn only later, when a recipe import fails, that a provider does not answer or cannot read images. Add a test that sends one real chat message, and reports whether the provider can read an image:

- POST /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/test tests an unsaved provider: the body is the same as for creating one. Nothing is saved.
- POST /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/{provider_id}/test tests a saved provider; an optional body of the same shape overrides its values for the test (a field that is not given, such as apiKey, keeps the saved value). An unknown id is a 404.
- Both need the can_manage permission (403 otherwise) and answer 200 with a result {success, message, supportsImages}, a new schema AIProviderTestResult (success, a bool; message, an optional string; supports_images, an optional bool that stays None when the image check did not run), exported with the other AI provider schemas. A failed test is a 200 too.

In OpenAIService:
- ping(provider, message, images=None) sends one chat message to the provider with the general.debug prompt, through get_response (response_schema OpenAIText, the images as attachments, the given provider), and returns its answer. The admin debug endpoint uses it too instead of its own copy of those steps.
- test_connection(provider) returns an AIProviderTestResult. It pings with a text message. If that raises, the result is success=False with a message naming only the error: the class name of the exception's __cause__ (or of the exception itself when it has none), followed by " (HTTP <status>)" when that error has a status_code, for example "NotFoundError (HTTP 404)" or "Exception". Never relay the provider's response text or error body (managers could aim base_url at an internal host); log the full error instead. An empty answer is success=False with message "No response received from the provider.". In both cases supports_images is None and no image is sent.
- After a successful text ping, ping again with a test image bundled with the service: a picture of a short recipe titled "Tomato & Egg Stir-Fry" (with a small data file next to it naming the keywords to look for). supports_images is True when the reply mentions the recipe (case-insensitive), False when it does not, when the reply is empty, or when that ping raises. A provider without image support is still success=True.

Add the frontend side as well: a Test button in the AI provider dialog that shows the result, the API client methods and types, and the English strings.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/services_tests tests/integration_tests/user_group_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 9 minutes).

frontend.text:
Bug: logging in to an embedded Mealie (in an iframe, over HTTPS) fails with a 500.

When Mealie runs inside another site, the frontend flags the request (the X-Mealie-Embedded header) and the server sets the session cookie with SameSite=None, Secure and Partitioned. Partitioned is not supported by the Python 3.12 standard library that Starlette uses to write cookies, so setting the cookie raises and every embedded login over HTTPS answers 500. The frontend asks for a partitioned cookie as well when it clears the token cookie.

Expected: drop Partitioned on both sides, keep everything else.
- Backend: session_cookie_attrs(request) returns no "partitioned" key in any case; secure and samesite stay as they are (embedded over HTTPS: samesite "none" and secure). set_session_cookie(response, request, token, expires_in, remember_me) then works for an embedded HTTPS request: its Set-Cookie header starts with mealie.access_token=<token>; and has SameSite=none and Secure, and no Partitioned.
- Frontend: getTokenCookieOptions() returns options without a partitioned property; its secure and sameSite values are unchanged. Update the comments that still describe a partitioned cookie.

Tests: backend `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests`; frontend `cd frontend && npx vitest run app/composables` (all frontend specs: `cd frontend && npx vitest run`). The whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 9 minutes).

fullstack.text:
Feature: tell the user why pasted recipe data could not be imported.

On the page that creates a recipe from pasted HTML or JSON, data Mealie cannot read (JSON without the schema.org Recipe declaration, malformed JSON, HTML with no recipe in it) gives no useful feedback. The streaming endpoint POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json/stream sends an error event whose message is only the exception's class name; POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json answers 400 with that same class name as detail.message; and the page shows nothing.

Expected, backend:
- The error event's message carries the reason when the failure is an HTTPException that has one: the "details" value of a dict detail (the scraper raises its ParserErrors values that way, for example {"details": "BAD_RECIPE_DATA"}), or the detail itself when it is a non-empty string. Any other exception keeps its class name.
- So for each of the three inputs above the stream still answers 200 and its first error event has message == ParserErrors.BAD_RECIPE_DATA.value, and the non-streaming endpoint answers 400 with detail.message == "BAD_RECIPE_DATA".

Expected, frontend:
- The recipe API client's create-from-HTML-or-JSON call always settles, exactly once, closing the stream: on the done event; on an error event, with the backend's message or "Recipe creation failed" when the payload is not a backend message; and when the stream closes without either event.
- The import page shows an error card when an import fails: only ld+json or microdata containing a schema.org Recipe can be imported, and pasted JSON must declare both "@context": "https://schema.org/" and "@type": "Recipe"; with links to Google's recipe structured-data docs, Mealie's GitHub issues and the schema.org Recipe page. Starting a new import clears it. Add the English string.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 9 minutes); frontend specs: `cd frontend && npx vitest run`.

security.text:
Security: two group and household endpoints are open to every member.

- GET /api/households/members returns the household's users, with their e-mail addresses and permissions, to any logged-in member of the household.
- PUT /api/groups/preferences lets any member of a group change the group's preferences.

Expected: both require the can_manage permission, checked the way the other management endpoints check it (the controller's permission checks); a user without it gets 403. Users with can_manage keep today's behaviour: the members list still holds exactly the household's own users. GET /api/groups/members stays as it is.

Frontend: the user profile page shows household statistics cards; hide the total-users card (totalUsers) from users who cannot manage, and keep the other cards.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests tests/integration_tests/user_group_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 9 minutes).
